topic: Memory Hierarchy and Caching Strategies: SRAM DRAM
explanation: The memory hierarchy is a tiered structure designed to optimize the trade-off between memory speed, capacity, and cost. High-speed, low-latency Static RAM (SRAM) constitutes the CPU cache levels (L1, L2, L3), positioned closest to the processor. Larger, slower Dynamic RAM (DRAM) serves as the main system memory. Caching strategies leverage the principle of locality of reference by storing copies of frequently accessed DRAM blocks in the faster SRAM caches. This mechanism significantly reduces the average memory access time (AMAT) and minimizes CPU stalls caused by high memory latency.
